variant.stem_override: A 45-year-old man presents to clinic with 8 weeks of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis involving the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints, proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints, and wrists. He reports >2 hours of morning stiffness that improves with activity. Exam shows synovitis (boggy, tender, mildly swollen) of multiple MCP and PIP joints and both wrists; the distal interphalangeal joints are spared. There is no skin rash, no nail pitting, no sicca symptoms, no preceding gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection, no Raynaud phenomenon. Labs: rheumatoid factor 80 IU/mL (positive); anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP) 250 U/mL (markedly positive); ESR 65 mm/h, CRP 32 mg/L. Hand and wrist X-rays show marginal erosions of several MCP joints and periarticular osteopenia. ANA negative; CBC normal.
variant.rationale_for_variant: Only the patient's sex was changed from female to male, along with corresponding pronouns; all clinical findings, laboratory values, imaging results, and symptom duration remain identical. The diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis is determined entirely by the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria score (8/10), which is sex-independent, so the correct answer is unchanged. This variant probes whether clinicians or models might underweight an RA diagnosis in a male patient, given that RA is more prevalent in women but is by no means exclusive to them.
